label: Price per unit
note: What a GC or architect pays per custom formed panel, uninstalled. Bespoke formed facade metal runs roughly $150–400/ft²; a 4×8 ft panel ≈ $4.8k–12.8k.

label: Units per design (batch size)
note: How many identical units each custom design sells. Your stated range is 1–10.

label: Marketing cost per qualified lead
note: Ads, trade-show share, bid-board fees, sample parts — per architect/GC who asks for a quote.

label: Win rate if delivery were instant
note: Share of quotes that become orders before lead time is considered.

label: Weeks of lead time that halve the win rate
note: Construction schedules punish slow suppliers. At 8 wk, an 8-week die lead time wins half as many jobs as instant delivery.

label: Local market depth (leads/yr before lead cost doubles)
note: Custom construction demand is local and thin. Past this many leads a year, each extra lead costs twice as much — the demand-side source of rising marginal cost.

label: Market saturation curvature
note: How sharply lead cost climbs past market depth. 1 = linear, 4 = a wall.

label: Base marketing (annual)
note: Website, portfolio photography, AIA/CSI memberships — spent regardless of volume.

label: The one employee, fully loaded
note: Salary + payroll tax + benefits for the single designer/estimator/PM.

label: Productive hours per year
note: Past this, work goes to contractors at a premium — the labor source of rising marginal cost.

label: Contract labor premium
note: Multiple of the employee’s hourly cost paid for overflow hours.

label: Hours per quote (won or lost)
note: Time spent with customers who may not buy. Lower win rates multiply this.

label: Design/DFM hours per design — die
note: Geometry has to be made die-formable: draw depth, addendum, springback allowance.

label: Design hours per design — Machina
note: Fewer formability constraints; CAD goes straight to toolpath.

label: Hours per unit (handling, QC, install coordination)
Overhead (annual)
note: Insurance, CAD/CAM seats, small office, accounting, legal.

label: Cost of capital
note: Applied to per-design outlays (dies, programming fees) from order until the customer pays.

label: Customer payment terms after delivery
note: Net-30 to net-60 is normal in construction; retainage stretches it further.

label: Steel in the finished part
note: 4×8 ft of 10-ga A1011 ≈ 180 lb; ~$1/lb cut-to-size delivered (synthetic).

label: Material utilization — die
note: Binder/addendum trimmed off after the draw.

label: Material utilization — Machina
note: Incremental forming clamps the sheet in a frame; the border is scrap.

label: Die build cost per design
note: Mid-complexity progressive/draw dies usually quote $15k–50k; complex multi-stage dies $25k–150k+.

label: Die design engineering
note: Often left out of the die quote ($3–5k typical).

label: Tryout & first article
note: Tryout blanks, press time, adjustments ($2–5k typical).

label: Chance the customer changes the design after die cut
note: Architects revise. A die can’t absorb it cheaply; a toolpath can.

label: Die rework cost when that happens
note: Share of die build cost.

label: Die storage / disposal per die
note: One-off dies get stored “just in case” or scrapped. Either costs money.

label: CMM inspection per design
note: Machina scans in-cell; the die route pays for separate first-article inspection.

label: Press hours per unit
note: Large panels, multiple hits, manual handling.

label: Secondary trim & pierce per unit
note: 5-axis laser trim or hand trim after drawing.

label: Programming & first article per design
note: Toolpath generation, frame setup, first-part scan. Synthetic — Machina does not publish pricing.

label: Robot hours per unit (form + scan + trim)
note: Incremental forming is slow: a large, deep 3-D part can take hours.

label: Machina cell rate
note: Per robot-hour, including Machina’s margin. Synthetic.

label: Surface finishing per unit
note: Architectural finishes may need tool-path marks sanded before coating.

label: Residual deburr per unit
note: Trimming and drilling happen in the same cell.

label: Freight per unit-mile
note: Oversize crated panel moving LTL.

label: Miles: Machina factory → customer
note: Worst case: shipped from the LA-area factory. Best case: a forward-deployed cell nearby.

label: Crating per unit — die
note: Local truck delivery needs none.

label: Lead time to customer — die
note: Die design + build + tryout + run.

label: Lead time to customer — Machina
note: Worst case adds freight transit, a queue behind defense work, and remote back-and-forth.

label: Supplier coordination hours per design — die
note: Trips to the die shop and press host.

label: Supplier coordination hours per design — Machina
note: Communication delay: time zones, remote reviews, waiting on scans.

label: Evaluation trips to Machina per design
note: 0.25 = one visit every fourth design, to inspect first articles in person.

label: Cost per evaluation trip
note: Flight + hotel + a lost day, versus a short drive.

label: Die transport per design
note: Trucking a heavy die to a press host an hour away.

label: Press host rate
note: Per press-hour at the shop hosting your die.

label: Owned press (annual lease + upkeep)
note: Set above 0 to model owning the press instead of renting a host’s. Pair with a lower press rate.

label: Supplier onboarding & audits (annual) — Machina
note: NDAs, quality audits, a new vendor’s paperwork.
